# a x + y of two limbs, a, x and y of the program, every limb guarded

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `axpy_entry_step_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $a x + y$:

$$z \approx a x + y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $a = a_0 + a_1$, $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axpy(a, x, y, z)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | `bool` | the step of the loop the function calls, once per element; not `constexpr`; rounds (loop `axpy_2_entry`; every limb of a, x and y guarded, rule R3 and its factors of a fused operation) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the functions are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/batch.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include; a view of `T` is taken where the table writes a view of `const T`. They take no marker: a function on arrays compiles only while the kernels of its loop are proved ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $a$ is normalized: $a_0 = \mathrm{RN}(a_0 + a_1)$.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 4u u)}{1 - 4u} + 4\right) u^2\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + 2\,\eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`; `kairn::traits` exports them rounded up to `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $\approx 8.6282 \times 10^{-32}$ | $\approx 2.4869 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1073} \approx 9.8813 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-148} \approx 2.8026 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.c000000000002p-104`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.c00004p-46f`, `0x1p-148f` |

The compiled constants are the entry `axpy` of `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 2>>`: `unit` and `tiny` bound the error relative to the sum of the magnitudes of the terms of the exact value ($\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert$ for $a x + y$; `reference` is `BoundForm::terms`); no bound relative to the computed value follows, and `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` are $+\infty$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `axpy_entry_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/MapSteps.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/MapSteps.v), against `axpy_entry_step_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions axpy_entry_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition axpy_entry_step_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a0 a1 x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec a0 a1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(z0, z1) := axpy_entry_step_2 emin prec tie_even a0 a1 x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - (((a0 + a1) * (x0 + x1)) + (y0 + y1))) <= (((3 * (1 + ((4 * u prec) * u prec))) / (1 - (4 * u prec))) + 4) * u prec ^ 2 * (Rabs ((a0 + a1) * (x0 + x1)) + Rabs (y0 + y1)) + 2 * eta emin.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `axpy_entry_step_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** axpy_step_2, mul_2_2 ([JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 12) then add_2_2 ([JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 6), on the guarded limbs of a, x and y (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation); bounds from [MR22](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#mr22). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/axpy_entry_step_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/axpy_entry_step_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`axpy_step_2`](axpy_step_2.md).

```
# The step of axpy_2_entry: axpy_step_2 on a scalar a and arrays x and y that the program supplies,
# every limb guarded first: those of y before they are added (rule R3), those of a and x because
# mul_2_2 takes them as factors of fused operations whose addends are not zero, where a compiler that
# sees the other factor to be 1 rewrites fma(x, 1, s) as x + s and may fuse a product of the program
# into it (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation: architecture.md; measured in the products of one
# limb, never in this one). Its claims are those of axpy_step_2: the guard is the identity on numbers
# of the format.
# Its bound, relative to the terms |a x| + |y|, from those of mul_2_2 and add_2_2, with
# eps+ = 3u^2/(1-4u): |z - (a x + y)| <= (eps+ (1 + 4u^2) + 4u^2) |a x| + eps+ |y| + (1 + eps+) 3/2 eta,
# the bound of dot_step_2, and (1 + eps+) 3/2 <= 2 from precision 4.

ga0      = guard(a0)
ga1      = guard(a1)
gx0      = guard(x0)
gx1      = guard(x1)
gy0      = guard(y0)
gy1      = guard(y1)
(z0, z1) = axpy_step_2(ga0, ga1, gx0, gx1, gy0, gy1)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the supplementary run of commit `8ee5ed9`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#axpy_entry_step_2)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled, supplementary run: 90 runners on 3 machines | 93 322 098 | 0 | 0.715573 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled, supplementary run: 90 runners on 3 machines | 93 350 052 | 0 | 0.700754 | no |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 3 domains of 3 formats | 1 616 493 | 0 | 0.417584 (`fp:5:-3:-2`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
